population.span: comparing two once-daily regimens of edoxaban with warfarin in 21,105 patients with moderate-to-high-risk atrial fibrillation (median follow-up, 2.8 years)

endpoint.span: The principal safety end point was major bleeding.

estimate.span: The annualized rate of major bleeding was 3.43% with warfarin versus 2.75% with high-dose edoxaban (hazard ratio, 0.80; 95% CI, 0.71 to 0.91; P<0.001)

entry_population_reading.span: Subjects with moderate or severe mitral stenosis, unresected atrial myxoma, or a mechanical heart valve

entry_population.extractor_why: Randomised adults (>=21 y) with documented AF and CHADS2 >=2; moderate/severe mitral stenosis and mechanical valves excluded, i.e. non-valvular AF.

extractor_mismatch_note: Served number (HR 0.80, 0.71-0.91) matches the abstract for major bleeding, high-dose edoxaban (60 mg) vs warfarin. However the served analysis_set label 'intention-to-treat' is not supported: the registry states major bleeding was analysed in the Safety Analysis set during the on-treatment period. The served row also silently selects the high-dose arm of a three-arm trial; the low-dose (30 mg) arm HR 0.47 (0.41-0.55) is a separate comparison against the same warfarin arm.
